newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Dlr pushes Hungary BUX up in positive mkt sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Dlr pushes Hungary BUX up in positive mkt sentiment.

text.p: A stronger dollar and recent earnings reports drove the Budapest Stock Exchange higher on Monday, traders said, but analysts said the market's near-term outlook was flat rather than bullish.

"The valuations were already reasonably stretched," said James Oates, director for central and east Europe at UBS in London. "People are trying to price in more growth into the market but we are pretty much at the top."
On Monday the BUX index closed at a preliminary 5,847.71 points, up 43.66 points or 0.75 percent.
"The strength of the dollar, and the strength of certain stocks, primarily Richter and MOL, drove the market higher," said Gyorgy Czipo of ING Barings.
At midday the Hungarian forint stood at 180.20/25 to the dollar, down from 182.00 at the opening.
Pharmaceuticals Richter surged to a new record level of 12,820 forints, before retreating to end at 12,700, up 390.

"Quite a strong foreign demand was generated at 12,500 forints," said Peter Nagy of Postabank Securities earlier. "Also, arbitrage has started between the spot and the futures market and arbitrage has also been driving it up."
Heavily traded oil company MOL edged up 30 forints to 3,250.
Both Richter and MOL are preparing for a new phase of their privatisation.

Traders said preliminary earnings reports by plastics maker Pannonplast on Thursday midnight and by home improvement product maker Graboplast on Friday afternoon, had positive impact on the market's sentiment.
Volumes were strong only for MOL and chemicals company TVK, with close to 300,000 shares traded in each.

Elsewhere on the market, meat processore Pick whose shareholders rejected an equity hike on Monday, closed unchanged at 11,200. Pannonplast ended at 9,000 forints, up 300; pharmaceuticals Egis at 11,750, up 150 and chemicals Borsodchem at 6,500, down 30.
The BUX index reached its highest level at 5,902.04 points on April 21.
